risks.note: The Company operates in a highly competitive environment where established global players with strong brands continue to invest significantly in R&D to drive innovation, while smaller regional players compete in price-sensitive segments with limited product offerings. Management's response is a balanced approach - standardised, fast-moving Super Abrasives and tooling products with targeted promotions for price-sensitive markets, and collaboration with international research institutions and partnerships with state-of-the-art technology providers for high-performance, quality-focused segments.
risks.risk: Two-sided competitive squeeze: global branded players out-spending on R&D at the top, regional price-led players at the bottom

risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as both opportunity and risk: failure to keep abreast of the latest technological changes could pose a competitive disadvantage and impair the Company's ability to meet customer demands. Mitigation is investment in R&D through an in-house DSIR-approved R&D facility focused on improving processes and products and developing innovative solutions for evolving customer needs.
risks.risk: Technology obsolescence - failure to keep pace with changing process automation, quality control, supply chain and customer-engagement technology

risks.note: Rated a material risk with negative financial implications: high attrition leads to loss of knowledge and expertise and reduced productivity, and damages the brand image and the ability to attract, develop, motivate and retain talent critical to business success. As an engineering, knowledge-based company, employees are described as its most precious assets. Mitigated via training and development programmes, job rotation to place the right person in the right job, performance-linked reward and recognition, and training to close appraisal gaps. Permanent-employee turnover rose to 8.49 in FY 2025-26 from 6.51 in FY 2024-25.
risks.risk: Employee attrition and skills loss in a knowledge-based engineering business

risks.note: The Company holds sensitive information including customer data, supplier information and intellectual property; a breach could cause significant reputational damage, financial loss and legal penalties, and loss of stakeholder trust. Cyber-attacks and data breaches are also called out under technology risk. Mitigation includes regular cybersecurity assessments, robust data security policies and procedures, and ongoing employee awareness and training programmes. Cybersecurity is one of the named risk categories in the enterprise risk framework.
risks.risk: Cybersecurity and data security breach exposure

risks.note: Air and water pollution, waste generation and disposal, climate change and resource scarcity can disrupt operations, and failure to comply with environmental regulations can lead to fines, penalties and legal action with reputational damage. The Company states it is not highly energy-intensive; mitigation includes investing in energy-efficient technologies, reducing emissions, improving water efficiency, an installed solar power plant, an Effluent Treatment Plant and Sewage Treatment Plant, a compliance management tool tracking all environmental regulations, and regular environmental monitoring.
risks.risk: Environmental footprint and regulatory compliance - air, water, waste, climate change and GHG emissions

risks.note: NSE and BSE levied monetary fines of Rs. 94,400 (inclusive of GST at 18%) for non-compliance with Regulation 17(1) of SEBI LODR for the quarter ended 31st December 2025; the Company has requested a waiver on the ground that compliance has since been met, following appointment of the Managing Director and CEO with effect from 19th January 2026. Corporate governance - board oversight, conflict of interest, ethics, risk and compliance - is itself listed as a material issue, since governance failures can undermine stakeholder trust, damage reputation and disrupt the business.
risks.risk: Governance and listing-compliance risk - a live regulatory lapse already penalised

risks.note: The auditors identified revenue recognition as a key audit matter because the Company has various customers with different terms of sales contracts, which increases the risk of error in the timing of revenue recognition; revenue is a key performance indicator watched by the Company and external stakeholders, so there is a risk of material misstatement. Revenue is recognised at a point in time on dispatch or delivery per contract terms.
risks.risk: Revenue-recognition complexity across a diverse contract base (auditor-designated key audit matter)

risks.note: The BRSR flags alignment with local communities as a material risk with negative financial implications - the business must be rooted in the community and aligned with its larger interests, and any adversarial relationship can impair the Company's ability to create long-term value. Approach is job creation, skill development, supporting local relief efforts, fostering local communities and paying taxes.
risks.risk: Community and social licence to operate
